name: R (ClientEarth) v Secretary of State for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (No. 1–3)

jurisdiction.court: UK Supreme Court; High Court of Justice of England and Wales (Administrative Court); with a preliminary ruling of the CJEU (Second Chamber)

at_issue: Adequacy and timing of the United Kingdom's national plans to bring NO2 levels within EU limit values.
abstract: Series of judicial review proceedings brought by ClientEarth over the United Kingdom's persistent breach of the NO2 limit values set by Directive 2008/50/EC. In 2013 the Supreme Court declared the UK in breach of Article 13 and referred questions to the CJEU, which held (C-404/13) that national courts must take any necessary measure to secure an air quality plan compliant with the Directive. In 2015 the Supreme Court issued a mandatory order requiring new plans within a court-approved timetable. The Administrative Court then quashed the 2015 plan, finding its compliance dates and over-optimistic emissions modelling unlawful, and in 2018 held the 2017 plan unlawful in part, ordering a supplement. The litigation is a leading example of iterative judicial supervision of air quality planning.

proceedings.title: Judgment [2013] UKSC 25
proceedings.outcome: Declaration that the UK was in breach of Article 13 of Directive 2008/50/EC; questions referred to the CJEU

proceedings.body: Court of Justice of the EU (Second Chamber)
proceedings.title: Preliminary ruling (C-404/13)
proceedings.outcome: Articles 13, 22, 23 and 30 of Directive 2008/50/EC interpreted; national courts must take any necessary measure, such as an order, to secure a compliant air quality plan

proceedings.title: Judgment [2015] UKSC 28
proceedings.outcome: Mandatory order requiring new air quality plans compliant with Article 23(1) within a court-approved timetable

proceedings.title: Judgment [2016] EWHC 2740 (Admin) (ClientEarth No. 2)
proceedings.outcome: 2015 air quality plan held unlawful and quashed

proceedings.title: Judgment [2018] EWHC 315 (Admin) (ClientEarth No. 3)
proceedings.outcome: 2017 plan held unlawful in part (45 local authority areas in England; no compliant plan for Wales); supplement to the plan ordered
